members.title: Greens gear up for fight with Labor as Sarah Hanson-Young pushes to strengthen laws to rein in big tech
members.lead: Minor party plans to drive a bargain in exchange for support for digital duty of care legislation Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast The Greens will push Labor to dramatically change new laws designed to rein in big tech, calling for individuals to have the right to take platforms to court and win financial compensation. As Labor prepares to introduce its planned digital duty of care laws into parliament this week, the Greens say they will drive a bargain in exchange for support, including pushing for fines by the eSafety commissioner to be levied as a percentage of corporations’ global revenue rather than set amounts. members.lead: Good morning, Krishani Dhanji with you here on our politics blog to cover another busy sitting week. Time is quickly running out for the government who have a few key pieces of legislation they want to pass with only three joint sitting weeks left in the year and one Senate-only sitting week. As my colleague Tom McIlroy has brought you this morning, Labor’s digital duty of care bill will be in the spotlight, with the Greens putting themselves at the negotiation table. They want bigger fines – a share of global revenue – for tech platforms that do the wrong thing.
